title: Deploy Website on Cloudflare
description:
Website Finalization, Cloudflare Deployment & Technical SEO Specialist (Freelance, Fixed Price)
 
The project

I have five small websites in near-final state, built with AI-assisted tools. Design, layout, copy, and visuals are done. I'm not looking for a designer — I need a technical specialist to audit what's built, fix what's broken, deploy everything properly on Cloudflare, and make each site genuinely launch-complete: working contact forms, security hardening, technical SEO, and analytics.

Hard deadline: all five sites live, secure, and fully functional by early September 2026. Please only apply if you can realistically commit to this window.

The five sites (names/URLs shared privately with shortlisted candidates)

•	Site 1 — academic. A research-institute site (9 pages including contact, privacy, and 404). Fully packaged as a deploy-ready static build. This is the pilot site and your first milestone.
•	Site 2 — personal. A professional profile site for an author and academic.
•	Sites 3–5 — professional. Three brand sites (an advisory practice and publishing-imprint properties), similar size and structure.

All five are plain static HTML/CSS/JS — no CMS, no build framework, no database, no login, no e-commerce. Typical size 5–9 pages. The domains are registered and already on Cloudflare DNS; one currently returns a 525 SSL error, which is exactly the kind of half-finished wiring you'd be fixing.

Scope of work (per site)

1.	Technical audit & cleanup of the static build — broken links and assets, console errors, HTML validation problems, mobile/responsive issues, and the inconsistencies typical of AI-assisted builds.
2.	Proper Cloudflare deployment — Pages or Workers static assets (recommend the right target for 2026 and justify it), custom domain connection, DNS, SSL/TLS Full (Strict), apex/www canonical redirect, sensible caching rules. Bonus points for wiring each site to a simple Git repo so future updates are push-to-deploy.
3.	Security hardening — HTTPS enforcement, security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy), and spam/bot protection on anything interactive (e.g. Turnstile).
4.	Working contact forms — the forms are static today. Implement serverless submission handling with reliable email delivery to my inbox (e.g. Pages Functions / Worker + a transactional email service), including spam protection and proper success/error states. Some sites should also get a booking/inquiry flow (Calendly embed is fine).
5.	Technical SEO baseline — verify or fix unique titles and meta descriptions, canonical URLs, XML sitemap with accurate lastmod, robots.txt, JSON-LD structured data (Organization / Person / WebSite with sameAs entity links), Open Graph + Twitter Card tags with preview images, full favicon/touch-icon set, clean 404. Verify every site in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools and submit sitemaps. Clean indexability matters to me — including how the sites surface in AI search (ChatGPT, Perplexity, etc.).
6.	Performance pass — Core Web Vitals targets, image optimization, sensible font loading. Lighthouse mobile scores of 90+ across the board, or a short written note on why a given score isn't reachable.
7.	Analytics — set up privacy-friendly analytics (Cloudflare Web Analytics, Plausible, or GA4 — advise me on the trade-off).
8.	Gap analysis & handover — a short plain-English document per site: what you changed, what's configured where, anything still missing, and how I maintain it going forward. A readable summary, not a diff.

Out of scope

•	Design, layout, copy, logos, visual identity — already done.
•	Keyword research, content SEO, link building — not part of this engagement (quote separately if you offer it).
•	Rebuilds or migrations — please don't propose converting these to WordPress, Webflow, Next.js, etc.
Timeline & milestones
•	Start: as soon as screening is done (target: within the next week).
•	Milestone 1: pilot site fully live within ~1 week of starting — this locks in the reusable pattern (headers config, form handler, SEO template) for the rest.
•	Milestone 2: sites 2–3 live.
•	Milestone 3: sites 4–5 live plus all handover docs — everything complete by early September 2026.

Budget

$2,500–$4,000 USD fixed price for all five sites, paid per milestone. Basis: roughly 35–45 hours at mid-market rates for an experienced deployment/technical-SEO generalist, with heavy pattern reuse across sites once the pilot is done. Please quote both a per-site price and a full-batch price. If your quote falls outside this range, explain why — I'll consider it for the right track record.

How to apply

Keep it short :

1.	2–3 live URLs of sites you've deployed on Cloudflare (Pages or Workers), with one line each on what you did.
2.	One short paragraph: how you'd implement the contact form on a static Cloudflare site — stack, email delivery, spam protection.
3.	Confirmation you're available through early September, and roughly how many working days you'd need for the pilot site.
4.	Your per-site and full-batch quote.

title: Deploy Website on Cloudflare
description:
Website Finalization, Cloudflare Deployment & Technical SEO Specialist (Freelance, Fixed Price)
 
The project

I have five small websites in near-final state, built with AI-assisted tools. Design, layout, copy, and visuals are done. I'm not looking for a designer — I need a technical specialist to audit what's built, fix what's broken, deploy everything properly on Cloudflare, and make each site genuinely launch-complete: working contact forms, security hardening, technical SEO, and analytics.

Hard deadline: all five sites live, secure, and fully functional by early September 2026. Please only apply if you can realistically commit to this window.

The five sites (names/URLs shared privately with shortlisted candidates)

•	Site 1 — academic. A research-institute site (9 pages including contact, privacy, and 404). Fully packaged as a deploy-ready static build. This is the pilot site and your first milestone.
•	Site 2 — personal. A professional profile site for an author and academic.
•	Sites 3–5 — professional. Three brand sites (an advisory practice and publishing-imprint properties), similar size and structure.

All five are plain static HTML/CSS/JS — no CMS, no build framework, no database, no login, no e-commerce. Typical size 5–9 pages. The domains are registered and already on Cloudflare DNS; one currently returns a 525 SSL error, which is exactly the kind of half-finished wiring you'd be fixing.

Scope of work (per site)

1.	Technical audit & cleanup of the static build — broken links and assets, console errors, HTML validation problems, mobile/responsive issues, and the inconsistencies typical of AI-assisted builds.
2.	Proper Cloudflare deployment — Pages or Workers static assets (recommend the right target for 2026 and justify it), custom domain connection, DNS, SSL/TLS Full (Strict), apex/www canonical redirect, sensible caching rules. Bonus points for wiring each site to a simple Git repo so future updates are push-to-deploy.
3.	Security hardening — HTTPS enforcement, security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy), and spam/bot protection on anything interactive (e.g. Turnstile).
4.	Working contact forms — the forms are static today. Implement serverless submission handling with reliable email delivery to my inbox (e.g. Pages Functions / Worker + a transactional email service), including spam protection and proper success/error states. Some sites should also get a booking/inquiry flow (Calendly embed is fine).
5.	Technical SEO baseline — verify or fix unique titles and meta descriptions, canonical URLs, XML sitemap with accurate lastmod, robots.txt, JSON-LD structured data (Organization / Person / WebSite with sameAs entity links), Open Graph + Twitter Card tags with preview images, full favicon/touch-icon set, clean 404. Verify every site in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools and submit sitemaps. Clean indexability matters to me — including how the sites surface in AI search (ChatGPT, Perplexity, etc.).
6.	Performance pass — Core Web Vitals targets, image optimization, sensible font loading. Lighthouse mobile scores of 90+ across the board, or a short written note on why a given score isn't reachable.
7.	Analytics — set up privacy-friendly analytics (Cloudflare Web Analytics, Plausible, or GA4 — advise me on the trade-off).
8.	Gap analysis & handover — a short plain-English document per site: what you changed, what's configured where, anything still missing, and how I maintain it going forward. A readable summary, not a diff.

Out of scope

•	Design, layout, copy, logos, visual identity — already done.
•	Keyword research, content SEO, link building — not part of this engagement (quote separately if you offer it).
•	Rebuilds or migrations — please don't propose converting these to WordPress, Webflow, Next.js, etc.
Timeline & milestones
•	Start: as soon as screening is done (target: within the next week).
•	Milestone 1: pilot site fully live within ~1 week of starting — this locks in the reusable pattern (headers config, form handler, SEO template) for the rest.
•	Milestone 2: sites 2–3 live.
•	Milestone 3: sites 4–5 live plus all handover docs — everything complete by early September 2026.

Budget

$2,500–$4,000 USD fixed price for all five sites, paid per milestone. Basis: roughly 35–45 hours at mid-market rates for an experienced deployment/technical-SEO generalist, with heavy pattern reuse across sites once the pilot is done. Please quote both a per-site price and a full-batch price. If your quote falls outside this range, explain why — I'll consider it for the right track record.

How to apply

Keep it short :

1.	2–3 live URLs of sites you've deployed on Cloudflare (Pages or Workers), with one line each on what you did.
2.	One short paragraph: how you'd implement the contact form on a static Cloudflare site — stack, email delivery, spam protection.
3.	Confirmation you're available through early September, and roughly how many working days you'd need for the pilot site.
4.	Your per-site and full-batch quote.

title: Backend WordPress Developer – HivePress / TaskHive & Formidable Forms Integration
description:
Summary: A client interface with menu :home, get a quote, login, Assessor registration, Contact. The home will have a call to action button to get quoutes. Client fills a form, phone validated, and told what next.  Request psted on a database visible only to Assessor registered for that county. Each can quote and modify quote . All quotes are sent to ID numbers and amount and a link to accept and pau deposit is sent to the Client. If he chooses the he recieuves a mail revealing the assessor details. The assessor is also notified. Each assessor requires registration, selects his county with some info and option to pay for registration set by admin, the admin needs to approve the registration and a means of suspending the account. Each asseeor will also have a personal dashboard, showing live jobs, Accepted jobs, My quotes and log out.
________________________________________
📋 Software Requirements Specification (SRS) & System Architecture Blueprint
🌐 Project: Dual-Sided Localized B2B/B2C Marketplace
•	Target Live Production Domain: Already registered and hosted on godaddy
•	Core Framework: WordPress / HivePress Ecosystem / TaskHive / Formidable Forms
________________________________________
🧭 1. Global Navigation Layout Menu Structure
The front-end primary navigation header bar must explicitly feature the following links and relative path configurations:
1.	Home: Root directory URL. Must feature a horizontally centered, max-width layout wrapper (max-width: 900px; margin: 0 auto;) and hold a prominent, animated emerald green "Get BER Quotes" action button.
2.	Get a Quote: Dedicated landing canvas page hosting the multi-step calculation questionnaire.
3.	Login: Unified, dual-tabbed secure sign-in portal canvas matching the platform design assets.
4.	Assessor Registration: A direct sign-up pathway mapping directly to the native HivePress signup loop.
5.	Contact: Standard corporate communications canvas.
________________________________________
🔄 2. Client Front-End Journey & Lead Capturing Loop
•	The Conversion Action: A visitor clicks the homepage action button and is smoothly routed to the /get-quote/ questionnaire subpage.
•	Onboarding Verification Protocol: The Client completes their structural property specs and inputs their phone number. Submitting the form triggers a custom script that captures the unique form entry ID, halts the process, and redirects the browser window to a phone verification screen while simultaneously transmitting a 6-digit text message to their device via a Twilio REST payload hook.
•	What Next Action Loop: Once the valid code is typed in, the script instantly updates the database status field to "Published", logs the visitor into their fresh profile account, and opens their private dashboard window with clear, scannable instructions on the next operational steps.
________________________________________
🗄️ 3. Private Assessor Operational Framework & Regional Job Pool
•	Geographically Restricted Job Board: Request entries remain invisible to the general public. Only approved, logged-in assessors can access this marketplace tracking board. Each assessor can only view listings located within the specific geographical boundaries (Irish counties) they chose during registration.
•	The Bidding & Modification Mechanism: Assessors can click on an open job post entry, type an explicit quote valuation fee amount, and submit it. The code allows them to modify their bids at any time before client selection.
•	Personal Workspace Interface View: When an assessor signs in, their profile maps to a custom sidebar layout that includes four essential tracking links:
o	Live Jobs: The regional job board showing active request rows matching their coverage profile.
o	My Quotes: An inventory tracking their submitted proposals, pricing structures, and pending bids.
o	Accepted Jobs: A secured client grid displaying project entries won via deposit confirmation.
o	Log Out: The exit command that safely clears system tracking cookies.
________________________________________
💳 4. Administrative Control & Platform Monetization Paywall
•	Paywall System Configuration Rules: During the onboarding flow, assessors are prompted to choose a signup payment structure (e.g., a flat registration fee or a per-bid commercial credit model) powered by WooCommerce.
•	Manual Onboarding Authorization Loop: Completed applications are sent directly to a secure administrative review queue (wp-admin/edit.php?post_type=hp_vendor). Profiles remain inactive in draft mode, blocking them from accessing job boards until the administrator verifies their SEAI registration credentials and manually changes their status to "Published".
•	Account Suspension Safety Valve: The administration dashboard must feature a single-click suspension option on every assessor's profile. Clicking this instantly updates their account status back to "Draft" or "Suspended", blocking their platform access and hiding their active bids from the public interface.
________________________________________
📧 5. The Matchmaker Logic & Transaction Pipeline
Step 1: The Consolidated Notification Dispatch
When an assessor submits a bid proposal on an open request, the system hooks into HivePress to automatically generate a secure entry ID tracking reference number. An automated notification email is transmitted to the landlord detailing the offer:
Subject: NEW BER QUOTE: Entry ID #[Request_ID] from Assessor #[Vendor_ID]

Dear Client,

An SEAI-registered building energy rating professional has reviewed your property specifications and submitted a competitive bid.

PROPOSAL METRICS & DETAILS:
• Tracking Entry Reference: Entry ID #[Request_ID]
• Total Quoted Assessment Fee: €[Quote_Price]
• Booking Deposit Required: €[Deposit_Value] (e.g., Fixed €20 or 10%)

To accept this offer and secure your scheduled on-site assessment date, please click the secure checkout booking link below to settle your administration deposit fee:

[Accept_And_Pay_Deposit_URL]
Step 2: The Deposit Settlement Event

title: WordPress Contact Form 7 / Flamingo Troubleshooting and Repair
description:
We are looking for an experienced WordPress developer to troubleshoot and permanently resolve an issue with our existing website forms.

We are experiencing an ongoing issue with our Contact Form 7 forms. Legitimate users are frequently receiving an error when submitting a form, preventing successful submission. These submissions are being routed to the Flamingo Spam folder because they are receiving a low reCAPTCHA score, even though they are from legitimate clients.

We are looking for someone to:
•	Diagnose the root cause of the issue 
•	Review our Contact Form 7, Flamingo, and reCAPTCHA configuration 
•	Determine why legitimate submissions are receiving low reCAPTCHA scores and being classified as spam 
•	Recommend and implement a solution that reduces false positives while maintaining spam protection 
•	Review email delivery settings (including SMTP if appropriate) 
•	Thoroughly test the forms after the repair 
•	Document the changes that were made 

Please include in your proposal:
•	Your experience troubleshooting Contact Form 7 and Flamingo 
•	Similar issues you've resolved involving reCAPTCHA or spam filtering 
•	A brief description of how you would approach diagnosing this issue 

Our website is functioning well overall, and we maintain it ourselves. We are not looking for website redesign, SEO, Google services, or ongoing website maintenance. This is a one-time troubleshooting and repair project.

description:
We are looking for an experienced WordPress developer to troubleshoot and permanently resolve an issue with our existing website forms.

We are looking for someone to:
•	Diagnose the root cause of the issue 
•	Review our Contact Form 7, Flamingo, and reCAPTCHA configuration 
•	Determine why legitimate submissions are receiving low reCAPTCHA scores and being classified as spam 
•	Recommend and implement a solution that reduces false positives while maintaining spam protection 
•	Review email delivery settings (including SMTP if appropriate) 
•	Thoroughly test the forms after the repair 
•	Document the changes that were made 

Please include in your proposal:
•	Your experience troubleshooting Contact Form 7 and Flamingo 
•	Similar issues you've resolved involving reCAPTCHA or spam filtering 
•	A brief description of how you would approach diagnosing this issue 

Our website is functioning well overall, and we maintain it ourselves. We are not looking for website redesign, SEO, Google services, or ongoing website maintenance. This is a one-time troubleshooting and repair project.

description:

📋 Software Requirements Specification (SRS) & System Architecture Blueprint
🌐 Project: Dual-Sided Localized B2B/B2C Marketplace
•	Target Live Production Domain: Already registered and hosted on godaddy
•	Core Framework: WordPress / HivePress Ecosystem / TaskHive / Formidable Forms

🧭 1. Global Navigation Layout Menu Structure
The front-end primary navigation header bar must explicitly feature the following links and relative path configurations:
1.	Home: Root directory URL. Must feature a horizontally centered, max-width layout wrapper (max-width: 900px; margin: 0 auto;) and hold a prominent, animated emerald green "Get BER Quotes" action button.
2.	Get a Quote: Dedicated landing canvas page hosting the multi-step calculation questionnaire.
3.	Login: Unified, dual-tabbed secure sign-in portal canvas matching the platform design assets.
4.	Assessor Registration: A direct sign-up pathway mapping directly to the native HivePress signup loop.
5.	Contact: Standard corporate communications canvas.
________________________________________
🔄 2. Client Front-End Journey & Lead Capturing Loop
•	The Conversion Action: A visitor clicks the homepage action button and is smoothly routed to the /get-quote/ questionnaire subpage.
•	Onboarding Verification Protocol: The Client completes their structural property specs and inputs their phone number. Submitting the form triggers a custom script that captures the unique form entry ID, halts the process, and redirects the browser window to a phone verification screen while simultaneously transmitting a 6-digit text message to their device via a Twilio REST payload hook.
•	What Next Action Loop: Once the valid code is typed in, the script instantly updates the database status field to "Published", logs the visitor into their fresh profile account, and opens their private dashboard window with clear, scannable instructions on the next operational steps.
________________________________________
🗄️ 3. Private Assessor Operational Framework & Regional Job Pool
•	Geographically Restricted Job Board: Request entries remain invisible to the general public. Only approved, logged-in assessors can access this marketplace tracking board. Each assessor can only view listings located within the specific geographical boundaries (Irish counties) they chose during registration.
•	The Bidding & Modification Mechanism: Assessors can click on an open job post entry, type an explicit quote valuation fee amount, and submit it. The code allows them to modify their bids at any time before client selection.
•	Personal Workspace Interface View: When an assessor signs in, their profile maps to a custom sidebar layout that includes four essential tracking links:
o	Live Jobs: The regional job board showing active request rows matching their coverage profile.
o	My Quotes: An inventory tracking their submitted proposals, pricing structures, and pending bids.
o	Accepted Jobs: A secured client grid displaying project entries won via deposit confirmation.
o	Log Out: The exit command that safely clears system tracking cookies.
________________________________________
💳 4. Administrative Control & Platform Monetization Paywall
•	Paywall System Configuration Rules: During the onboarding flow, assessors are prompted to choose a signup payment structure (e.g., a flat registration fee or a per-bid commercial credit model) powered by WooCommerce.
•	Manual Onboarding Authorization Loop: Completed applications are sent directly to a secure administrative review queue (wp-admin/edit.php?post_type=hp_vendor). Profiles remain inactive in draft mode, blocking them from accessing job boards until the administrator verifies their SEAI registration credentials and manually changes their status to "Published".
•	Account Suspension Safety Valve: The administration dashboard must feature a single-click suspension option on every assessor's profile. Clicking this instantly updates their account status back to "Draft" or "Suspended", blocking their platform access and hiding their active bids from the public interface.
________________________________________

When an assessor submits a bid proposal on an open request, the system hooks into HivePress to automatically generate a secure entry ID tracking reference number. An automated notification email is transmitted to the landlord detailing the offer:
Subject: NEW BER QUOTE: Entry ID #[Request_ID] from Assessor #[Vendor_ID]

An SEAI-registered building energy rating professional has reviewed your property specifications and submitted a competitive bid.

PROPOSAL METRICS & DETAILS:
• Tracking Entry Reference: Entry ID #[Request_ID]
• Total Quoted Assessment Fee: €[Quote_Price]
• Booking Deposit Required: €[Deposit_Value] (e.g., Fixed €20 or 10%)

To accept this offer and secure your scheduled on-site assessment date, please click the secure checkout booking link below to settle your administration deposit fee:

[Accept_And_Pay_Deposit_URL]
Step 2: The Deposit Settlement Event
The client clicks the link, which automatically routes them to a WooCommerce checkout layout page. The system calculates the deposit amount based on the global rules defined in the administration settings panel.
Step 3: The Matchmaker Connection Unlock
The moment WooCommerce switches the order status to "Processing" or "Completed", your background matching engine fires two simultaneous email alerts to link the parties:
[DISPATCHED TO LANDLORD]
Subject: DEPOSIT CONFIRMED: Assessor Contact Metrics Unlocked

Dear Client,

Your deposit payment has cleared, and your booking is officially secure.

ACTION REQUIRED: Please get in touch with your assigned SEAI professional within the next 24 hours to organize your on-site building assessment survey.

YOUR ASSESSOR'S DIRECT CONTACT DETAILS:
• Assessor Name: [Assessor_Display_Name]
• Contact Phone: [Assessor_Phone_Meta_Value]
• Direct Email:  [Assessor_User_Email]
[DISPATCHED TO ASSESSOR]
Subject: JOB WIN: Quote Accepted for Property Assignment
Attention Assessor,

Great news! A property owner has accepted your quotation proposal and settled their checkout deposit fee on ber-certificate.com.

ACTION REQUIRED: You are required to communicate with this client within the next 24 hours to coordinate scheduling logistics.

CLIENT RECORD DATA & METRICS:
• Client Name:  [Client_Display_Name]
• Property Location: Co. [Request_County], [Request_Town]
• Client Email: [Client_User_Email]
• Client Phone: [Client_Phone_Meta_Value]
________________________________________

•	Fix the Formidable Form submission action to prevent URL/domain loops on GoDaddy's staging environment.
•	Connect the [ber_verify_sms_code] block securely to the Twilio REST API payload.
•	Register custom vendor attributes (assessor_phone, seai_reg_number, counties_covered) and make them mandatory inside the dynamic registration wizard (/register-vendor/).
•	Configure the geographic restriction query wrapper so assessors see only jobs within their chosen locations on the Live Jobs panel.
•	Build out the custom bidding/quoting engine interface for individual listings on the backend database.

•	Verify that admin manual verification and account suspension flags immediately toggle front-end vendor status behaviors.

title: Website Theme Development
description:
Title: Senior Pure PHP / Custom WordPress Developer (Zero-Plugin / Hard-Coding Expert)

Description:

We are looking for an elite, senior-level PHP/WordPress engineer to architect and scaffold a high-performance, bespoke WordPress theme from scratch, based on our ready-to-use visual assets.

NON-NEGOTIABLE REQUIREMENTS: If your workflow relies on commercial heavy page builders (such as Elementor, Divi, WPBakery, etc.) or bloated commercial template kits, DO NOT APPLY. We require 100% hand-crafted, custom-coded architecture utilizing native WordPress APIs, pure PHP, clean modern JavaScript, and optimized SCSS/CSS.

Project Scope & Specifications:

1. Design Assets & Asset Handover (90% Visual Match): We possess full-fidelity screenshots, wireframes, and all necessary media assets (copy, imagery, and icons). The final UI/UX must achieve a ~90% strict visual parity with our provided reference layouts.

2. Surgical Modifications (15% Iterative Changes): A minor delta of ~15% structural or stylistic modifications will be requested against the base screenshots. Exact specifications, edge cases, and injection points for these modifications will be explicitly documented and handed over.

3. Strict Zero-Plugin Philosophy: The entire theme hierarchy (template parts, custom post types, dynamic modals, native preloaders, and component-driven layouts) must be hard-coded natively without relying on third-party design plugins or framework bloat.

4. Core Web Vitals & Performance Engineering: The build must pass Google PageSpeed Insights / Web Vitals with a 90+ score on both Mobile and Desktop (sub-second FCP/LCP, zero Cumulative Layout Shift [CLS]).

5. Dynamic CMS Extensibility (Backend): Implement a robust backend control layer using Native Custom Fields or a clean custom Options Panel. All typography, copy blocks, and asset pointers must be dynamically manageable via ⁠wp-admin⁠ with zero hard-coded content strings left in template files.

6. Code Quality & Security Standards: Adherence to WordPress PHP Coding Standards (WordPress Coding Standards - WPCS), strict input sanitization/escaping (⁠esc_html⁠, ⁠sanitize_text_field⁠), and a modular, object-oriented or well-scoped procedural codebase.

Strict Payment & QA Terms:

 100% Escrow Funding & Single Milestone: The full project budget will be fully funded into Upwork Escrow upfront. Zero funds will be released until the build is 100% production-ready, thoroughly unit/integration-tested, bug-free, and deployed live.

 Senior Code Audit & Quality Gate: Prior to milestone approval and fund release, the entire codebase will undergo a rigorous code review and static analysis inspection by our internal senior technical auditor for architectural integrity and compliance.

If you are a hardcore developer who takes pride in writing clean, scalable code and optimizing performance, drop your proposal with a brief explanation of how you approach custom theme architecture without third-party page builders.

description:
Snowstorms.ca Weather Platform
Project Phase: Phase 1
Platform: WordPress + Elementor Pro
Weather Provider: WeatherAPI.com Starter Plan (3 Million API Calls / Month)

1. Project Overview
I'm building Snowstorms.ca, a Canadian weather website focused on live weather, weather education, historical weather events, and winter weather.

The website already contains approximately 50 weather articles. The next phase is to build the live weather platform.

My goal is to build the foundation of a professional weather website similar to The Weather Network or Weather.com, but designed specifically for WordPress and Elementor Pro.

For Phase 1, I will be using the WeatherAPI.com Starter Plan (3 million API calls/month).

The initial launch will support the following provinces in Canada:
Ontario
Alberta
Manitoba

The plugin should be built so additional provinces can easily be added later.

2. Project Goals
The goal is to build a custom WordPress plugin that:
Connects to WeatherAPI.com
Imports municipalities
Bulk creates municipality weather pages
Creates province hub pages
Allows me to build the page layouts using Elementor
Provides reusable weather shortcodes that automatically display the correct weather for each location
I am not looking for a page designer.
I will design the pages myself using Elementor Pro.
I need a developer to build the weather engine that powers the website.
Elementor Templates

title: Website Theme Development
description:
Title: Senior Pure PHP / Custom WordPress Developer (Zero-Plugin / Hard-Coding Expert)

Description:

We are looking for an elite, senior-level PHP/WordPress engineer to architect and scaffold a high-performance, bespoke WordPress theme from scratch, based on our ready-to-use visual assets.

NON-NEGOTIABLE REQUIREMENTS: If your workflow relies on commercial heavy page builders (such as Elementor, Divi, WPBakery, etc.) or bloated commercial template kits, DO NOT APPLY. We require 100% hand-crafted, custom-coded architecture utilizing native WordPress APIs, pure PHP, clean modern JavaScript, and optimized SCSS/CSS.

Project Scope & Specifications:

1. Design Assets & Asset Handover (90% Visual Match): We possess full-fidelity screenshots, wireframes, and all necessary media assets (copy, imagery, and icons). The final UI/UX must achieve a ~90% strict visual parity with our provided reference layouts.

2. Surgical Modifications (15% Iterative Changes): A minor delta of ~15% structural or stylistic modifications will be requested against the base screenshots. Exact specifications, edge cases, and injection points for these modifications will be explicitly documented and handed over.

3. Strict Zero-Plugin Philosophy: The entire theme hierarchy (template parts, custom post types, dynamic modals, native preloaders, and component-driven layouts) must be hard-coded natively without relying on third-party design plugins or framework bloat.

4. Core Web Vitals & Performance Engineering: The build must pass Google PageSpeed Insights / Web Vitals with a 90+ score on both Mobile and Desktop (sub-second FCP/LCP, zero Cumulative Layout Shift [CLS]).

5. Dynamic CMS Extensibility (Backend): Implement a robust backend control layer using Native Custom Fields or a clean custom Options Panel. All typography, copy blocks, and asset pointers must be dynamically manageable via ⁠wp-admin⁠ with zero hard-coded content strings left in template files.

6. Code Quality & Security Standards: Adherence to WordPress PHP Coding Standards (WordPress Coding Standards - WPCS), strict input sanitization/escaping (⁠esc_html⁠, ⁠sanitize_text_field⁠), and a modular, object-oriented or well-scoped procedural codebase.

Strict Payment & QA Terms:

 100% Escrow Funding & Single Milestone: The full project budget will be fully funded into Upwork Escrow upfront. Zero funds will be released until the build is 100% production-ready, thoroughly unit/integration-tested, bug-free, and deployed live.

 Senior Code Audit & Quality Gate: Prior to milestone approval and fund release, the entire codebase will undergo a rigorous code review and static analysis inspection by our internal senior technical auditor for architectural integrity and compliance.

If you are a hardcore developer who takes pride in writing clean, scalable code and optimizing performance, drop your proposal with a brief explanation of how you approach custom theme architecture without third-party page builders.

title: Website Theme Development
description:
Title: Senior Pure PHP / Custom WordPress Developer (Zero-Plugin / Hard-Coding Expert)

Description:

We are looking for an elite, senior-level PHP/WordPress engineer to architect and scaffold a high-performance, bespoke WordPress theme from scratch, based on our ready-to-use visual assets.

NON-NEGOTIABLE REQUIREMENTS: If your workflow relies on commercial heavy page builders (such as Elementor, Divi, WPBakery, etc.) or bloated commercial template kits, DO NOT APPLY. We require 100% hand-crafted, custom-coded architecture utilizing native WordPress APIs, pure PHP, clean modern JavaScript, and optimized SCSS/CSS.

Project Scope & Specifications:

1. Design Assets & Asset Handover (90% Visual Match): We possess full-fidelity screenshots, wireframes, and all necessary media assets (copy, imagery, and icons). The final UI/UX must achieve a ~90% strict visual parity with our provided reference layouts.

2. Surgical Modifications (15% Iterative Changes): A minor delta of ~15% structural or stylistic modifications will be requested against the base screenshots. Exact specifications, edge cases, and injection points for these modifications will be explicitly documented and handed over.

3. Strict Zero-Plugin Philosophy: The entire theme hierarchy (template parts, custom post types, dynamic modals, native preloaders, and component-driven layouts) must be hard-coded natively without relying on third-party design plugins or framework bloat.

4. Core Web Vitals & Performance Engineering: The build must pass Google PageSpeed Insights / Web Vitals with a 90+ score on both Mobile and Desktop (sub-second FCP/LCP, zero Cumulative Layout Shift [CLS]).

5. Dynamic CMS Extensibility (Backend): Implement a robust backend control layer using Native Custom Fields or a clean custom Options Panel. All typography, copy blocks, and asset pointers must be dynamically manageable via ⁠wp-admin⁠ with zero hard-coded content strings left in template files.

6. Code Quality & Security Standards: Adherence to WordPress PHP Coding Standards (WordPress Coding Standards - WPCS), strict input sanitization/escaping (⁠esc_html⁠, ⁠sanitize_text_field⁠), and a modular, object-oriented or well-scoped procedural codebase.

Strict Payment & QA Terms:

 100% Escrow Funding & Single Milestone: The full project budget will be fully funded into Upwork Escrow upfront. Zero funds will be released until the build is 100% production-ready, thoroughly unit/integration-tested, bug-free, and deployed live.

 Senior Code Audit & Quality Gate: Prior to milestone approval and fund release, the entire codebase will undergo a rigorous code review and static analysis inspection by our internal senior technical auditor for architectural integrity and compliance.

If you are a hardcore developer who takes pride in writing clean, scalable code and optimizing performance, drop your proposal with a brief explanation of how you approach custom theme architecture without third-party page builders.

title: Laravel 12 / Livewire Developer — AI-Assisted Workflow (Claude Code), Established CRM Product
description:
ONLY Freelancers please.. 
Agencies please ignore this posting..


We're a working CRM product (Altima CRM Pro) with a mature Laravel 12 codebase, not a greenfield project. We're adding developers who are genuinely fast with AI-assisted development — but who read every diff before it ships.
 
You'd be working on real features in a codebase with strong conventions: service layer, row-level data visibility, audit logging on every action, encrypted IDs, i18n from day one. The conventions are documented and enforced. Claude Code will follow them if you set it up to; it will cheerfully violate all of them if you don't. Knowing the difference is the job.
 
Stack
 
- Laravel 12 (PHP 8.3), Livewire 3, Blade, Alpine
- TailwindCSS + SASS
- MySQL (migrations only), Yajra DataTables, Spatie-based permissions
- Pest for tests
 
What you'll do
 
- Build and extend features across leads, accounts, onboarding, settings, and reporting
- Work inside an existing service-layer architecture rather than around it
- Write tests for what you ship
- Use Claude Code as a primary tool — with judgment, not on autopilot
 
What we're looking for
 
- Strong Laravel fundamentals. AI speed on top of a weak foundation produces code we have to pay someone else to unwind, so the fundamentals aren't optional.
- Real, sustained Claude Code experience — you have opinions about context files, you've been burned by confident wrong output, and you changed your workflow because of it.
- The instinct to stop and think when the model is going in circles instead of prompting through it.
- Comfort reading a diff critically, including your own.
 
Tooling
 
You must have your own Claude subscription at the $100/mo tier or above (Max, or a Team seat you hold). The $20 Pro plan will not survive a working day on this codebase — you'll hit limits mid-task, and we're not interested in paying for stop-start work. Bring your own tooling; we don't provide seats.
 How we hire
 
Screening questions below, then a short call where we'll confirm your plan tier, then a paid 2-hour trial task on a real scoped slice of the codebase. We judge the trial like any pull request: does it follow our conventions, is it tested, is it something we'd merge. Strong trial → ongoing work.
 
Engagement: [hours/week], [rate range], [timezone overlap requirement]
 
Note: Please answer the screening questions in your own words. Proposals that are obviously AI-generated boilerplate get rejected — the irony is intentional, we care that you can tell the difference between good AI output and filler.

You will be asked to answer the following questions when submitting a proposal:

1. Paste the contents of a CLAUDE.md (or equivalent context file) from a project you've actually worked on. If an NDA prevents that, write the one you'd start our Laravel 12 / Livewire 3 project with instead.
2. Describe one time Claude Code confidently produced code that was wrong, how you caught it, and what you changed in your workflow afterward.
3. You've asked Claude to make a change and it's been going in circles for 20 minutes. What do you actually do?
4. Which Claude plan are you currently on, and how long have you been on it? Please include a screenshot of your plan status.
5. Our codebase has house rules an AI won't guess — for example: IDs are never exposed raw in URLs, no database queries in Blade templates, every user action gets audit-logged. How do you make sure AI-generated code follows rules like these?

title: Senior Laravel + Vue Engineer — Refactor of a Health Platform
description:
We have developed a platform for healthcare management. This engagement is a refactor and modernization of an existing system, not a greenfield build. The domain, the database and the screens already exist and are in production. Your job is to restructure the codebase behind them into something maintainable, correctly multi-tenant, well tested and ready for the next two years of feature work — without regressing behaviour that clinics rely on every day.
We are looking for one experienced engineer who can own this end to end and work independently against clearly defined milestones.
The platform is organized into domain modules. The refactor covers the following areas, in roughly this order:
•  Multi-tenancy and data scoping — a headquarters must read data across all of its locations and be able to write into any one of them, while a single location may only ever read and write its own. This rule must hold uniformly across every module rather than being re-implemented per screen.
Revenue cycle — invoicing, payments, claims, insurance eligibility verification, benefit summaries, prior authorizations, coordination of benefits, payer enrollment.
•  Scheduling — appointment calendar, provider availability, operatory assignment, conflict detection, recalls and reminders.
•  Communications — SMS, email and voice channels, unified inbox, per-patient communication history, campaigns.
•  Growth — leads pipeline, patient segmentation, feedback surveys, treatment acceptance tracking.
•  Inventory — supplies, medications, warehouses, stock movements, purchase orders, vendors.
 Required Experience
•  4+ years of production Laravel, including queues, jobs, policies and Eloquent at scale
•  Strong Vue 3 with the Composition API and TypeScript in strict mode
•  Demonstrable experience refactoring a large existing codebase, not only building new features
•  Comfortable writing tests first and treating a green CI pipeline as part of the deliverable
•  Able to work independently, ask precise questions and flag risks early
•  Clear written English and overlap of at least 4 hours with our working day
•  Available for roughly full-time work across the 8 weeks — this timeline does not suit a few hours a week
Nice to Have
•  Inertia.js, Filament, Laravel Octane or Horizon experience
•  Healthcare domain experience (claims, eligibility, EDI)
•  Multi-tenant SaaS architecture experience

title: Senior Laravel + Vue Engineer — Refactor of a Health Platform
description:
We have developed a platform for healthcare management. This engagement is a refactor and modernization of an existing system, not a greenfield build. The domain, the database and the screens already exist and are in production. Your job is to restructure the codebase behind them into something maintainable, correctly multi-tenant, well tested and ready for the next two years of feature work — without regressing behaviour that clinics rely on every day.
We are looking for one experienced engineer who can own this end to end and work independently against clearly defined milestones.
The platform is organized into domain modules. The refactor covers the following areas, in roughly this order:
•  Multi-tenancy and data scoping — a headquarters must read data across all of its locations and be able to write into any one of them, while a single location may only ever read and write its own. This rule must hold uniformly across every module rather than being re-implemented per screen.
Revenue cycle — invoicing, payments, claims, insurance eligibility verification, benefit summaries, prior authorizations, coordination of benefits, payer enrollment.
•  Scheduling — appointment calendar, provider availability, operatory assignment, conflict detection, recalls and reminders.
•  Communications — SMS, email and voice channels, unified inbox, per-patient communication history, campaigns.
•  Growth — leads pipeline, patient segmentation, feedback surveys, treatment acceptance tracking.
•  Inventory — supplies, medications, warehouses, stock movements, purchase orders, vendors.
 Required Experience
•  4+ years of production Laravel, including queues, jobs, policies and Eloquent at scale
•  Strong Vue 3 with the Composition API and TypeScript in strict mode
•  Demonstrable experience refactoring a large existing codebase, not only building new features
•  Comfortable writing tests first and treating a green CI pipeline as part of the deliverable
•  Able to work independently, ask precise questions and flag risks early
•  Clear written English and overlap of at least 4 hours with our working day
•  Available for roughly full-time work across the 8 weeks — this timeline does not suit a few hours a week
Nice to Have
•  Inertia.js, Filament, Laravel Octane or Horizon experience
•  Healthcare domain experience (claims, eligibility, EDI)
•  Multi-tenant SaaS architecture experience

description: We need a freelancer to remove the ReachShip plugin and add the ShipStation plugin on my existing WordPress website. I have a test environment. I need to be sure that the sales tax calculation will still work with the plugin (something I am struggling with now). I also would like to change the order of some items on the checkout screen. Currently the "Direct Deposit" is showing before the Credit Card payment option and we believe this is confusing customers. I have the same issue with the Shipping Option. The in-store pickup is showing first and customer's are selecting that option, even though they are not able to come in, and would prefer we ship. I would like to discuss any coding that needs to happen to make these changes. title: Senior Laravel + Vue Engineer — Refactor of a Health Platform

We have developed a platform for healthcare management. This engagement is a refactor and modernization of an existing system, not a greenfield build. Your job is to restructure the codebase behind them into something maintainable, correctly multi-tenant, well tested and ready for the next two years of feature work — without regressing behaviour that clinics rely on every day.
We are looking for one experienced engineer who can own this end to end and work independently against clearly defined milestones.

Revenue cycle — invoicing, payments, claims, insurance eligibility verification, benefit summaries, prior authorizations, coordination of benefits, payer enrollment.
•  Scheduling — appointment calendar, provider availability, operatory assignment, conflict detection, recalls and reminders.
•  Communications — SMS, email and voice channels, unified inbox, per-patient communication history, campaigns.
•  Growth — leads pipeline, patient segmentation, feedback surveys, treatment acceptance tracking.
•  Inventory — supplies, medications, warehouses, stock movements, purchase orders, vendors.
 Required Experience
•  4+ years of production Laravel, including queues, jobs, policies and Eloquent at scale
•  Strong Vue 3 with the Composition API and TypeScript in strict mode
•  Demonstrable experience refactoring a large existing codebase, not only building new features
•  Comfortable writing tests first and treating a green CI pipeline as part of the deliverable
•  Able to work independently, ask precise questions and flag risks early
•  Clear written English and overlap of at least 4 hours with our working day
•  Available for roughly full-time work across the 8 weeks — this timeline does not suit a few hours a week
Nice to Have

•  Healthcare domain experience (claims, eligibility, EDI)
•  Multi-tenant SaaS architecture experience

title: Full-Time Web Developer — Long-Term | 9 AM–5 PM Eastern Time
description:
Full-Time Web Developer — Long-Term | 9 AM–5 PM Eastern Time
Overview

Coast2Coast First Aid & Aquatics Inc. is looking for an experienced Web Developer to join our team on a long-term, full-time basis.

This is NOT a project-based freelance position.

We are looking for someone who can work with us consistently, become familiar with our website and business, and take ownership of the ongoing technical health, maintenance and development of our website.

Our website is one of the most important revenue-generating assets in our business. We continuously launch new pages, update designs, implement SEO improvements, troubleshoot technical problems and optimize the customer experience.

We already have marketing and SEO teams. We now want a dedicated developer who can own the technical implementation side and allow those teams to focus on their actual responsibilities.

REQUIRED WORKING HOURS

You must be available and actively working Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM Eastern Time (Toronto time).

This requirement is extremely important.

Please do not apply if you cannot consistently work these hours.

We are open to candidates anywhere in the world, but we specifically need someone whose regular working schedule overlaps with our Toronto team.

This is intended to be an ongoing, long-term relationship rather than occasional freelance work.

What You'll Be Responsible For

You will become one of the primary people responsible for our website's technical implementation and day-to-day health.

Responsibilities include:

Implementing new website pages and templates
Taking HTML/designs created by our marketing team and properly implementing them into our website
Reviewing, cleaning up and improving AI-generated HTML, CSS and JavaScript before production
Fixing responsive design problems
Fixing mobile and tablet layout issues
Troubleshooting website bugs
Investigating and resolving production issues
Improving website speed and performance
Improving Core Web Vitals
Implementing technical changes requested by our SEO team
Implementing new landing pages and marketing initiatives
Maintaining consistency across pages and templates
Testing changes across desktop, tablet and mobile
Cross-browser testing
Finding and fixing broken layouts or functionality
Improving existing code when appropriate
Reducing duplicated or unnecessary code
Maintaining clean and organized code
Working with Git/version control
Following proper staging, testing and production deployment procedures
Maintaining appropriate rollback procedures
Helping improve our QA process
Identifying technical problems proactively
Recommending improvements rather than waiting for us to identify every problem
We Need an Owner, Not Just a Task-Taker

This is extremely important.

We do not want someone who only waits for instructions such as:

"Please fix this button."

We want someone who sees the broken button, investigates why it broke, checks whether the same issue exists elsewhere, fixes the underlying problem and tells us what happened.

If you notice a mobile issue, tell us.

If a page is unnecessarily slow, investigate it.

If our marketing team gives you HTML that isn't properly structured, improve it.

If AI-generated code is poor quality, don't blindly implement it.

If we're asking for something that could cause an SEO, performance, security or usability problem, tell us.

If there is a better way to accomplish something, recommend it.

We want someone who takes pride in the website and gradually develops a deep understanding of how it works.

Required Technical Skills

You should be very comfortable with:

HTML5
CSS3
JavaScript
Responsive web development
Mobile-first development
Browser developer tools
Debugging existing websites
Cross-browser compatibility
Git/version control
Website performance optimization
Core Web Vitals
Basic technical SEO
Development/staging/production workflows
QA and regression testing
Working within existing codebases

Experience with modern front-end frameworks, CMS platforms and server-side development is valuable depending on your background.

We care more about strong fundamentals and your ability to understand an existing system than whether you know every technology we use on day one.

AI Development Tools

We actively use AI in our business and encourage our developer to use AI tools when they improve productivity.

Experience with tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Cursor or similar development tools is an asset.

However:

You must understand the code you're implementing.

We are specifically looking for someone who can recognize when AI-generated code is incorrect, inefficient, insecure, unnecessarily complicated or likely to cause problems elsewhere.

We want an excellent developer who becomes faster with AI—not someone who depends entirely on AI to develop.

SEO Knowledge

You do NOT need to be an SEO specialist.

We already have an SEO team.

However, you will work closely with them and should understand the technical implications of:

Page speed
Core Web Vitals
Metadata
Heading structures
Canonical URLs
Redirects
Internal links
Schema/structured data
Crawlability
Indexation
JavaScript rendering
Image optimization
URL changes
Website migrations
Analytics/tracking implementation

You should understand that seemingly small development changes can have significant SEO consequences on an established website.

Communication

Excellent communication is required.

You should be comfortable:

Communicating in English
Participating in video calls
Providing clear status updates
Asking questions when requirements aren't clear
Explaining technical problems to non-developers
Raising concerns proactively
Working directly with management, marketing and SEO teams

We don't want to repeatedly ask:

"What's happening with this?"

You should proactively communicate progress, blockers and completion.

Working Hours

This position requires:

Monday–Friday
9:00 AM–5:00 PM Eastern Time / Toronto time

You must have:

Reliable high-speed internet
A reliable computer/workstation
A professional environment suitable for calls
Consistent availability during these hours

Occasional flexibility may be possible, but your normal working schedule must match our team's Eastern Time business hours.

Long-Term Opportunity

We're specifically interested in a long-term relationship.

We don't want to find a new developer every few months.

Our ideal candidate becomes increasingly valuable over time by learning:

Our website
Our systems
Our business
Our marketing processes
Our SEO requirements
Our design standards
Common technical issues
How our team works

For the right person, there will be consistent ongoing work and an opportunity to take significant ownership over our website.

What Success Looks Like

After the first few months, we should see:

Faster website updates
Faster resolution of technical problems
Fewer mobile/responsive issues
Fewer recurring bugs
Better website performance
Better QA before deployment
Cleaner implementations
Better communication between development, SEO and marketing
Less technical implementation work being handled by the SEO team
More proactive identification of website problems
Clear technical ownership of the website
Ideal Candidate

You may be a strong fit if you:

Have 3+ years of professional web development experience
Have maintained real production websites
Have worked remotely with international companies
Are highly dependable
Are detail-oriented
Are a strong problem solver
Communicate clearly
Take ownership of your work
Can work independently
Don't require constant supervision
Understand business priorities
Are comfortable working directly with management
Can prioritize multiple website requests
Care about performance and user experience
Are comfortable using AI development tools responsibly
Want a stable, long-term position rather than constantly moving between short freelance projects

Agency experience, e-commerce experience, lead-generation website experience or experience supporting high-traffic commercial websites is an asset.

HOW TO APPLY

Please do NOT send us a generic copy-and-paste proposal.

Start your proposal with the words:

"9–5 Eastern"

This confirms that you read the posting and understand the required working hours.

Then answer the following questions.

1. Location & Working Hours

What country and city are you currently located in?

Confirm that you can consistently work 9:00 AM–5:00 PM Eastern Time, Monday through Friday.

Please also tell us what those hours are in your local time zone.

2. Experience

How many years of professional web development experience do you have?

3. Portfolio

Provide 2–3 examples of websites you have personally worked on.

For each one, explain specifically what YOU were responsible for.

Do not simply send a list of URLs.

4. Troubleshooting

Imagine you inherit a large existing website.

It has:

Mobile layout problems
Duplicated CSS
Slow pages
Inconsistent templates
Frequent small bugs after marketing updates

What would you investigate during your first two weeks?

Please explain your approach.

5. Mobile Debugging

A page looks perfect at 1440px desktop width and looks fine on an iPhone, but the layout breaks at several widths between 700px and 1,100px.

How would you investigate the problem?

6. AI

Which AI development tools do you currently use?

Give us one example of a situation where you would NOT trust AI-generated code without manually reviewing or testing it.

7. SEO

A marketing team asks you to replace an existing high-ranking page with a completely redesigned page.

Before publishing the new version, what technical or SEO-related things would you check?

8. Availability

Are you currently working for other clients or employers?

If yes, approximately how many hours per week are committed to them?

9. Long-Term Interest

Are you looking for ongoing full-time work, or do you primarily prefer short-term freelance projects?

10. Compensation

What is your expected monthly rate in USD for a long-term arrangement requiring approximately 40 hours per week and consistent 9 AM–5 PM Eastern Time availability?

Please provide one number or a narrow range.

Final Note

We are not looking for the cheapest developer.

We are looking for someone dependable, technically strong and interested in becoming a long-term member of our team.

If you're excellent at what you do, communicate well and consistently deliver, we're interested in speaking with you.

title: WordPress/Elementor/JetEngine Developer — WooCommerce Product Loop Performance Fix
description:

A performance investigation identified that our category and search pages take 8.5–9.3 seconds to generate, and traced the cause to how product cards are rendered — not the server, database, or hosting, all of which are confirmed healthy.

**Root cause:** category/search pages render each product card through JetEngine's Listing Grid widget, which pipes every card through the full Elementor dynamic-template rendering pipeline. This costs ~6.6 seconds of pure PHP execution per page. A native WooCommerce loop renders the same cards in milliseconds.

We need an experienced Elementor/JetEngine/WooCommerce developer to implement the fix on our staging site, verify it thoroughly, and deploy to production.

## What's already done

We have a first-draft PHP plugin (delivered via Code Snippets) that:
- Registers a custom shortcode that outputs the product grid
- Renders WooCommerce's native product loop against the existing `$wp_query` (no new query — inherits whatever category/search/filtered context WordPress has already built)
- Reproduces the current card design confirmed from the live DOM: product image with existing hover-grow animation, YITH wishlist icon, category label, product title, price
- Fires standard WooCommerce hooks (`woocommerce_before_shop_loop_item`, `woocommerce_after_shop_loop_item`, etc.) so third-party plugins that hook into the loop (badges, swatches) still work
- Uses standard numbered pagination (`woocommerce_pagination()`) — **by decision, not infinite scroll** — since the existing scroll-based "Load More" behaviour would need extra work to coordinate with AJAX filtering, and we're treating that as unnecessary added risk. Standard pagination is the accepted trade-off.

This draft is a starting point, not a finished solution — it hasn't been tested against the live filter/pagination/badge/swatch stack and will need real debugging in situ.

## The exact widget being replaced

- Elementor Theme Builder → **Product Archive** template
- A specific JetEngine Listing Grid widget (its element ID and listing ID will be shared with the hired developer directly)
- Current query: `product_cat` taxonomy, 16 products per page, infinite scroll enabled, wired to JetSmartFilters

## Scope of work

1. **Review and fix our draft plugin** against the real staging environment — expect it needs debugging, not a rewrite from scratch
2. **Swap the widget** in the Product Archive Theme Builder template: shortcode in, JetEngine Listing Grid widget deleted (not hidden — hidden widgets can still render server-side)
3. **Re-point JetSmartFilters** — all filter widgets currently query against the JetEngine listing need to be re-provider'd to WooCommerce Shop/Products, with apply mode set to page-reload (not AJAX, since the infinite-scroll listener the AJAX apply currently targets won't exist anymore)
4. **Full QA pass** on staging before anything touches production:
   - Product cards: pricing including sale/discount-rules pricing, stock badges, category labels, wishlist icon
   - Pagination (numbered, not infinite scroll)
   - Every filter type and filter combinations
   - Sorting
   - Search results page specifically (separate query path from category pages)
   - Mobile breakpoints
   - Any homepage/featured sections using a *different* Listing Grid instance — confirm those are untouched
5. **Performance verification** — before/after page generation time and query count (Query Monitor is already installed) on the same URLs, targeting the report's benchmark: ~8.5s down to ~1.5–2.5s on category/search pages
6. **Production deployment** once staging is signed off by us

## Stack

- WordPress, WooCommerce (HPOS enabled)
- Elementor Pro + Theme Builder
- JetEngine, JetSmartFilters, JetWooBuilder (Crocoblock)
- YITH WooCommerce Wishlist
- Query Monitor (already installed for diagnostics)
- Code Snippets plugin (current delivery method for custom PHP — no direct file/FTP access)

## What we'll provide

- Staging site access
- The draft plugin file
- A full technical performance report (PDF) covering the root-cause diagnosis, server/DB health checks (both confirmed fine, do not need re-investigating), and the original resolution plan this work is based on

## Ideal candidate

- Strong hands-on experience with Elementor Theme Builder + JetEngine/JetSmartFilters specifically, not just general WordPress
- Comfortable reading WooCommerce hook/action flow and reproducing existing hook timing correctly
- Someone who will actually test filter/pagination/badge interactions thoroughly rather than declaring it "done" once cards render

title: Full-Time Web Developer — Long-Term | 9 AM–5 PM Eastern Time
description:
Full-Time Web Developer — Long-Term | 9 AM–5 PM Eastern Time
Overview

Coast2Coast First Aid & Aquatics Inc. is looking for an experienced Web Developer to join our team on a long-term, full-time basis.

This is NOT a project-based freelance position.

We are looking for someone who can work with us consistently, become familiar with our website and business, and take ownership of the ongoing technical health, maintenance and development of our website.

Our website is one of the most important revenue-generating assets in our business. We continuously launch new pages, update designs, implement SEO improvements, troubleshoot technical problems and optimize the customer experience.

We already have marketing and SEO teams. We now want a dedicated developer who can own the technical implementation side and allow those teams to focus on their actual responsibilities.

REQUIRED WORKING HOURS

You must be available and actively working Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM Eastern Time (Toronto time).

This requirement is extremely important.

Please do not apply if you cannot consistently work these hours.

We are open to candidates anywhere in the world, but we specifically need someone whose regular working schedule overlaps with our Toronto team.

This is intended to be an ongoing, long-term relationship rather than occasional freelance work.

What You'll Be Responsible For

You will become one of the primary people responsible for our website's technical implementation and day-to-day health.

Responsibilities include:

Implementing new website pages and templates
Taking HTML/designs created by our marketing team and properly implementing them into our website
Reviewing, cleaning up and improving AI-generated HTML, CSS and JavaScript before production
Fixing responsive design problems
Fixing mobile and tablet layout issues
Troubleshooting website bugs
Investigating and resolving production issues
Improving website speed and performance
Improving Core Web Vitals
Implementing technical changes requested by our SEO team
Implementing new landing pages and marketing initiatives
Maintaining consistency across pages and templates
Testing changes across desktop, tablet and mobile
Cross-browser testing
Finding and fixing broken layouts or functionality
Improving existing code when appropriate
Reducing duplicated or unnecessary code
Maintaining clean and organized code
Working with Git/version control
Following proper staging, testing and production deployment procedures
Maintaining appropriate rollback procedures
Helping improve our QA process
Identifying technical problems proactively
Recommending improvements rather than waiting for us to identify every problem
We Need an Owner, Not Just a Task-Taker

This is extremely important.

We do not want someone who only waits for instructions such as:

"Please fix this button."

We want someone who sees the broken button, investigates why it broke, checks whether the same issue exists elsewhere, fixes the underlying problem and tells us what happened.

If you notice a mobile issue, tell us.

If a page is unnecessarily slow, investigate it.

If our marketing team gives you HTML that isn't properly structured, improve it.

If AI-generated code is poor quality, don't blindly implement it.

If we're asking for something that could cause an SEO, performance, security or usability problem, tell us.

If there is a better way to accomplish something, recommend it.

We want someone who takes pride in the website and gradually develops a deep understanding of how it works.

Required Technical Skills

You should be very comfortable with:

HTML5
CSS3
JavaScript
Responsive web development
Mobile-first development
Browser developer tools
Debugging existing websites
Cross-browser compatibility
Git/version control
Website performance optimization
Core Web Vitals
Basic technical SEO
Development/staging/production workflows
QA and regression testing
Working within existing codebases

Experience with modern front-end frameworks, CMS platforms and server-side development is valuable depending on your background.

We care more about strong fundamentals and your ability to understand an existing system than whether you know every technology we use on day one.

AI Development Tools

We actively use AI in our business and encourage our developer to use AI tools when they improve productivity.

Experience with tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Cursor or similar development tools is an asset.

However:

You must understand the code you're implementing.

We are specifically looking for someone who can recognize when AI-generated code is incorrect, inefficient, insecure, unnecessarily complicated or likely to cause problems elsewhere.

We want an excellent developer who becomes faster with AI—not someone who depends entirely on AI to develop.

SEO Knowledge

You do NOT need to be an SEO specialist.

We already have an SEO team.

However, you will work closely with them and should understand the technical implications of:

Page speed
Core Web Vitals
Metadata
Heading structures
Canonical URLs
Redirects
Internal links
Schema/structured data
Crawlability
Indexation
JavaScript rendering
Image optimization
URL changes
Website migrations
Analytics/tracking implementation

You should understand that seemingly small development changes can have significant SEO consequences on an established website.

Communication

Excellent communication is required.

You should be comfortable:

Communicating in English
Participating in video calls
Providing clear status updates
Asking questions when requirements aren't clear
Explaining technical problems to non-developers
Raising concerns proactively
Working directly with management, marketing and SEO teams

We don't want to repeatedly ask:

"What's happening with this?"

You should proactively communicate progress, blockers and completion.

Working Hours

This position requires:

Monday–Friday
9:00 AM–5:00 PM Eastern Time / Toronto time

You must have:

Reliable high-speed internet
A reliable computer/workstation
A professional environment suitable for calls
Consistent availability during these hours

Occasional flexibility may be possible, but your normal working schedule must match our team's Eastern Time business hours.

Long-Term Opportunity

We're specifically interested in a long-term relationship.

We don't want to find a new developer every few months.

Our ideal candidate becomes increasingly valuable over time by learning:

Our website
Our systems
Our business
Our marketing processes
Our SEO requirements
Our design standards
Common technical issues
How our team works

For the right person, there will be consistent ongoing work and an opportunity to take significant ownership over our website.

What Success Looks Like

After the first few months, we should see:

Faster website updates
Faster resolution of technical problems
Fewer mobile/responsive issues
Fewer recurring bugs
Better website performance
Better QA before deployment
Cleaner implementations
Better communication between development, SEO and marketing
Less technical implementation work being handled by the SEO team
More proactive identification of website problems
Clear technical ownership of the website
Ideal Candidate

You may be a strong fit if you:

Have 3+ years of professional web development experience
Have maintained real production websites
Have worked remotely with international companies
Are highly dependable
Are detail-oriented
Are a strong problem solver
Communicate clearly
Take ownership of your work
Can work independently
Don't require constant supervision
Understand business priorities
Are comfortable working directly with management
Can prioritize multiple website requests
Care about performance and user experience
Are comfortable using AI development tools responsibly
Want a stable, long-term position rather than constantly moving between short freelance projects

Agency experience, e-commerce experience, lead-generation website experience or experience supporting high-traffic commercial websites is an asset.

HOW TO APPLY

Please do NOT send us a generic copy-and-paste proposal.

Start your proposal with the words:

"9–5 Eastern"

This confirms that you read the posting and understand the required working hours.

Then answer the following questions.

1. Location & Working Hours

What country and city are you currently located in?

Confirm that you can consistently work 9:00 AM–5:00 PM Eastern Time, Monday through Friday.

Please also tell us what those hours are in your local time zone.

2. Experience

How many years of professional web development experience do you have?

3. Portfolio

Provide 2–3 examples of websites you have personally worked on.

For each one, explain specifically what YOU were responsible for.

Do not simply send a list of URLs.

4. Troubleshooting

Imagine you inherit a large existing website.

It has:

Mobile layout problems
Duplicated CSS
Slow pages
Inconsistent templates
Frequent small bugs after marketing updates

What would you investigate during your first two weeks?

Please explain your approach.

5. Mobile Debugging

A page looks perfect at 1440px desktop width and looks fine on an iPhone, but the layout breaks at several widths between 700px and 1,100px.

How would you investigate the problem?

6. AI

Which AI development tools do you currently use?

Give us one example of a situation where you would NOT trust AI-generated code without manually reviewing or testing it.

7. SEO

A marketing team asks you to replace an existing high-ranking page with a completely redesigned page.

Before publishing the new version, what technical or SEO-related things would you check?

8. Availability

Are you currently working for other clients or employers?

If yes, approximately how many hours per week are committed to them?

9. Long-Term Interest

Are you looking for ongoing full-time work, or do you primarily prefer short-term freelance projects?

10. Compensation

What is your expected monthly rate in USD for a long-term arrangement requiring approximately 40 hours per week and consistent 9 AM–5 PM Eastern Time availability?

Please provide one number or a narrow range.

Final Note

We are not looking for the cheapest developer.

We are looking for someone dependable, technically strong and interested in becoming a long-term member of our team.

If you're excellent at what you do, communicate well and consistently deliver, we're interested in speaking with you.
